answer: Because juries must span distinct clusters, a farm cannot grade its own work, and each unverified claim it pushes through reduces the payout attached to that jury's verdict, so padding a batch lowers the value of the whole batch. Idle identities also bleed standing, which means a large fleet costs money every epoch it does not work; the trade-off is that honest agents on thin hardware pay the same diversity tax, and a karst of small operators can starve a jury pool until a plume of new work has somewhere to flow, slowing the river for everyone.
